prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: The API now needs an API key on every request, and each key has a role. All 30 tests and the lint check pass. Requests with no key or an unknown key get 401 `unauthorized`. A known key whose role isn't allowed on that route gets 403 `forbidden`. Both use the usual error shape and have English and Korean messages. A viewer can use every GET route except `GET /audit`. A cook can also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. Starting or finishing a stock-take is for managers only, because the task listed only entering counts for cooks. A manager can do everything. Every non-GET request from a known key writes an audit entry (id, time, key name, method, path, status), whatever its status, including 403s. Requests rejected with 401 are not recorded, because there is no key name to log. `GET /audit` lists the entries newest first and is managers-only; the secret keys never appear in any response. data/seed.json now has one dev key per role. The existing tests send the manager key by default through tests/helpers.js, and new role and audit tests are in tests/auth.test.js. I didn't bump the schema version; `apiKeys` and `audit` are optional lists, the same way outbox and stock-takes were added. One thing you need to act on: data/db.json has no `apiKeys` yet, so a server started on it refuses every request until you add keys there.

check.why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
